name: application-magic-link-sent-state
title: Magic Link Sent State
description: Confirmation panel shown after sending a passwordless sign-in link: echoes the destination email, disables resend behind a countdown, and offers a change-email fallback.
useWhen: Confirming to the user that a passwordless sign-in link or one-time code was emailed to them.
You want to prevent resend spam with a visible countdown rather than silently disabling the button.
The user needs a quick way to correct a mistyped email address without restarting the whole flow.
avoidWhen: The flow uses a code the user types back in (rather than a clicked link) — pair Input OTP or Two-Factor Setup instead.
You need a generic success message with no resend/timing behavior — a simple Alert is enough.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a fixed-width card centered in its container at all widths; text wraps naturally and the button remains full-width.
accessibility: The destination email is rendered as visible text (not just implied), so screen reader users get positive confirmation of where the link was sent.
The resend button's disabled state and its countdown label update together, so the reason it's unavailable is always stated in the button's own text, not conveyed by disabled styling alone.
"Change it" is a real button/link, not a decorative label, so keyboard and screen reader users can act on a mistyped address.

variants.title: Magic Link Sent State
variants.description: An envelope icon, 'Check your email' heading, the echoed email address, a disabled 'Resend link in 0:45' button, and a 'Wrong email? Change it' link.
accessibility: The countdown is expressed in the button's own visible text so its meaning doesn't depend on a separate live region.

variants.title: Magic Link Sent State (Dark)
variants.description: The same confirmation panel adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Icon, heading, and disabled-button contrast remain legible against the dark surface.
